BiblicalUsage: Ra'ash is the shaking of the earth itself — the quaking, the rattling, the uproar. At Horeb the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and after the wind an earthquake; and after the earthquake a fire — but the LORD was not in the earthquake. Amos dates his prophecy by it: 'two years before the earthquake.'
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the earthquake shows God's power without being God's voice: He shakes the mountains, yet He speaks in the still small voice that follows.
